message.content:
Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most acclaimed crime‑thrillers released (or widely available) in 2020, along with a short note on why they stood out:

| # | Title | Director | Why it’s worth watching |
|---|-------|----------|------------------------|
| 1 | **Tenet** | Christopher Nolan | A mind‑bending heist thriller that blends high‑concept time manipulation with slick action sequences. |
| 2 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Ritchie's signature fast‑paced style shines in this stylish gangster caper about a British drug lord trying to sell his empire. |
| 3 | **Uncut Gems** | Josh & Benny Safdie | Adam Sandler delivers an intense performance as a charismatic jeweler whose risky bets spiral into chaos. |
| 4 | **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Though released earlier, its 2020 Netflix premiere brought new audiences to Scorsese’s epic saga of mob life spanning decades. |
| 5 | **The Night Clerk** | David M. Rosenthal | A tense psychological thriller where a hotel clerk becomes entangled in a murder investigation after witnessing something suspicious. |
| 6 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | A Danish drama that turns into a gripping thriller when a man is falsely accused of child abuse, sparking a dangerous hunt. |
| 7 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | A modern retelling of the classic horror story, but with a strong crime‑thriller edge as the protagonist fights to prove her abuser’s existence. |
| 8 | **The Last Full Measure** | James Gray | A biographical crime‑drama that follows a Vietnam veteran who seeks justice for a fellow soldier’s death, blending courtroom tension with investigative intrigue. |

These films cover a range of styles—from Nolan’s cerebral spectacle to the gritty realism of the Safdie brothers—making them great picks whether you’re looking for high‑concept thrills or grounded storytelling.
